Numeric values and bit positions of enqueue, dequeue, scheduler flag, task state, priority and timer mode constants referenced by name.
Locking contract and ordering for enqueue, dequeue, replenish, throttle, migration and statistics paths beyond the two asserted runqueue holdings and the global table internal lock.
Behavior of unrouted helpers for runqueue clock, task lookup, bandwidth add or subtract, frequency update, timer primitives, time conversion, tree handling and priority handling.
State machines for server versus task entities, boosting, yielding, reclaim participation, inactive timer firing and bandwidth timer callback.
Overflow scaling factors, bandwidth shift widths, ratio normalization and density computation inputs.
Tracing, latency accounting and global heap removal and lookup paths not shown in routed fragments.

findings.text: Exposes a predicate that reports whether a deadline scheduling entity has exhausted its remaining execution budget, returning true when no budget remains.
Exposes a helper that converts raw execution time into capacity adjusted time, selecting a reclaim path for reclaim flagged entities and a frequency plus capacity scaling path otherwise.

Exposes wait interval finalization that derives elapsed wait from runqueue clock and a stored start stamp, with a distinct preservation path for migrating tasks and normal peak plus tally plus total accumulation otherwise.

Exposes sleeper enqueue accounting that folds prior sleep and block intervals into totals, maintains peaks, emits latency and trace signals, and adds separate wait totals when the task waited for input output.
Exposes bandwidth contribution helpers that add an entity share to total and active bandwidth, skipping specially marked entities and delegating to narrower helpers.
Exposes cancellation helpers for deadline related timers, where successful cancellation from outside the callback releases the associated task reference for non server entities.
Exposes runqueue count maintenance and global deadline publication, incrementing per runqueue and system running counts and refreshing the earliest deadline tracking structures.
Global deadline table update acts as a cross processor coordination point where a caller publishes one processor latest earliest deadline and the table inserts or refreshes that processor heap entry.
Capacity adjusted execution conversion acts as a charging point where scheduler accounting asks for the billable duration corresponding to observed execution on a given runqueue.
Scheduler statistics macros exist in active and inert variants, so the same call sites either mutate counters or expand to no operation depending on build configuration.

Timer arming chooses between a deferred reservation target derived from deadline minus remaining budget and a periodic target derived from the next period, then shifts the target by the offset between monotonic time and runqueue clock.
Periodic progression is defined so the next period equals the current absolute deadline adjusted by relative deadline and period parameters.
Reclaim scaling selects between full entity share and residual system headroom after inactive plus extra bandwidth, then applies ratio and bandwidth normalization before scaling the execution delta.

Enqueue validates that the entity is not already queued, records enqueue statistics, applies a constrained deadline check for non throttled entities with explicit deadlines, and restores bandwidth on restore or migrating arrivals.

Replenishment guarantees forward progress by repeatedly postponing the absolute deadline by one period and crediting one runtime while budget remains non positive, then repairs lagged deadlines through a fresh period and handles yield and defer flags.
Constrained deadline activation throttles when the runqueue clock lies strictly after the absolute deadline but before the next period, arming the timer and zeroing positive remaining budget.

Wakeup parameter handling distinguishes past deadline or overflow cases requiring a fresh period, a revised wakeup path for constrained or defer running entities still before deadline, and a defer arming path for eligible servers that retain their deadline.

Contending transition is skipped for zero runtime boosted placeholders, adds total bandwidth on migrated arrival, and either clears a pending non contending marker with timer cancellation or restores active bandwidth.
Dequeue statistics close an open wait interval for non current tasks and stamp sleep or block start times according to the observed task state when the dequeue reason indicates sleeping.
Enqueue statistics only act on wakeup arrivals and delegate sleeper interval folding to the generic sleeper helper with the entity owning task and its statistics block.
Statistics lookup yields no block when statistics are disabled or when the entity represents a scheduling server, otherwise it yields the owning task statistics.
Runqueue to entity navigation resolves the owning runqueue differently for server entities versus task backed entities, and queue membership is tested through emptiness of the tree linkage.
Earliest deadline cache only moves to a smaller deadline and its first insertion also raises the runqueue priority class, with every change mirrored into the global deadline table.
Deadline timer arming and active bandwidth mutation require the owning runqueue lock to be held, asserted at entry, which also serializes the timer queued check against concurrent expiry handling.
Global deadline table mutation holds the table internal spinlock with interrupt state saved, covering both insertion of a previously absent processor and refresh of an existing heap slot.

Deadline entity carries absolute and relative timing, remaining and maximum budget, bandwidth share and density, throttle and yield and defer related flags, runqueue linkage, tree linkage, and two timer objects.
Deadline runqueue carries total and active and extra and maximum bandwidth plus a scaling ratio, a deadline ordered tree with cached earliest entry, a running count, and an earliest deadline cache.
Scheduler statistics block carries wait lifecycle data including start stamp and peak and count and total, alongside sleep and block start stamps and peaks and totals plus input output wait totals.
Global deadline table carries a heap array of per slot deadline and processor number, a per processor reverse index into that heap, a size count, a free processor mask, and an internal lock.
Enqueue moves among direct enqueue, early return for throttled non replenish arrivals, timer armed throttled wait, cancellation plus unthrottle when the timer could not arm, and final tree insertion.
Replenish plus defer cycles among fresh period setup, budget restoration, deferred arming with throttling, timer driven wake, and clearing of armed and throttled markers.

Heap maintenance moves among absent processor insertion with size growth and mask clearing, present processor value refresh, upward repair, and a directional choice between upward and downward repair.
Wait and sleep accounting moves among wait start, wait end with peak and total update, sleep or block start on dequeueing sleep, and interval folding on wakeup enqueue.
Arming a timer in the past is rejected without queuing, and only a transition from unqueued to queued acquires a task reference, preserving balanced acquisition and release across concurrent expiry.

Bandwidth addition guards against counter wrap and against active exceeding total, overflow comparison uses scaled down time to avoid wide multiplication overflow, and negative sleep deltas are clamped to zero.
Replenishment warns once when the deadline remains in the past after catch up and then resets to a fresh period, while revised wakeup asserts that its deadline is not already past.
Migrating tasks preserve accumulated wait as a pending start value instead of emitting accounting, and absent processor heap slots are detected through a distinguished invalid index before insertion.
